items.title: Godfrey Hirsch Interview, 1987-11-10
items.q: But Jimmy Boyle was not a good drummer. He was at the Liberty Theater. He was not a great drummer. He was a very handsome guy.

ctx.x: I'm talking about when you were growing up and learning to play drums in town.

It was Paul Detrite. Paul Detrite. He was at the Orphium Theater. Uh-huh. Then Gosley. Adrian Gosley. He was always at one of the shows. Uh-huh. But Jimmy Boyle was not a good drummer. He was at the Liberty Theater. He was not a great drummer. He was a very handsome guy. He looked like Adolf Nenju. And he wore, always wore a white suit. Except at one time he was at the Liberty Theater when a rat got caught in one of the fans up there. The rat got torn to pieces and there was blood all over his white suit. Oh!…

items.title: Godfrey Hirsch Interview, 1987-10-27
items.q: Vit Lubowski, Tony Perranti, Tony Popalia, Jimmy, Jimmy, Boyle, the drummer. Johnny Karooge on fiddle. And Henry Connect I think was playing trumpet. And I think Tug Popalia was playing trombone. I'm not sure. And that's how I got to know these guys.

ctx.x: Well, did they have any fakers out there? No?

No, they were all readers. They played overtures and things like that. Overtures and played, that's how I got to know all this crap. I mean, in fact, when I went to this, when I was in high school, I got a job at the Liberty Theater as an usher working just weekends in high school during the school season. I think we got a dollar or two dollars a day. And you'd always get tips on Saturday and Sunday when you'd have an over crowd of people and you'd get people to sit. You have one of these flash boxes with green…
That's a trick. They don't know that you made a mistake.
